# Resource node API research (Phase 4, Task 6)

Recorded 2026-08-24. Read-only research only — no enumeration code written
yet. Per PLAN.md's "Critical Development Rule" for Phase 4 and CLAUDE.md's
"Claude Behavior for Uncertain APIs," this documents what the installed
`Source/FactoryGame/` headers actually declare, with file:line citations,
before any implementation is attempted.

## Important caveat: this is a header-only SDK

Every `.cpp` file under `Source/FactoryGame/Private/Resources/` opens with:

```cpp
// This file has been automatically generated by the Unreal Header Implementation tool
```

(confirmed at `Source/FactoryGame/Private/Resources/FGResourceNodeBase.cpp:1`
and `FGResourceNodeManager.cpp:1`), and the function bodies are stubs, e.g.:

```cpp
// Source/FactoryGame/Private/Resources/FGResourceNodeManager.cpp:5
AFGResourceNodeManager* AFGResourceNodeManager::Get(UWorld* world){ return nullptr; }
```

with every other method in that file similarly stubbed (`return nullptr;`,
`return EResourcePurity();`, empty bodies, etc. — `FGResourceNodeManager.cpp:5-26`).

This is a **header-distribution SDK**: the *declared API surface* (class
shapes, `UPROPERTY`/`UFUNCTION` signatures, enum values, doc comments) is
real and matches the installed game version, so it's trustworthy for
compiling against and for understanding what's *supposed* to exist. But
none of the actual runtime logic is present in this repo, so nothing below
can be verified by tracing real behavior — only by the declared shape. Any
claim about actual runtime semantics (e.g. "does `AFGResourceNodeManager`
really populate `mResourceNodes` at world load") must be verified by
logging real values in-game (Phase 4's own validation step), not by reading
these stub bodies.

## 1. Resource node actor class

- **`AFGResourceNodeBase`** — `Source/FactoryGame/Public/Resources/FGResourceNodeBase.h:92-323`.
  Base class `AFGStaticReplicatedActor` (`Source/FactoryGame/Public/Replication/FGStaticReplicatedActor.h:16`,
  itself an `AActor`), plus interfaces `IFGExtractableResourceInterface`,
  `IFGUseableInterface`, `IFGSaveInterface`, `IFGSignificanceInterface`,
  `IFGClearanceInterface`.
- **`AFGResourceNode`** (`Source/FactoryGame/Public/Resources/FGResourceNode.h:65-198`)
  — subclass adding purity/amount (still `Abstract`). Further specialized by
  `AFGResourceNodeFrackingCore`, `AFGResourceNodeFrackingSatellite`,
  `AFGResourceNodeGeyser`.
- Resource type: `TSubclassOf<UFGResourceDescriptor> mResourceClass`
  (`FGResourceNodeBase.h:250`), read via `GetResourceClass()` (`:144`) /
  `GetResourceClassOriginal()` (`:150`); an override channel also exists
  (`mResourceClassOverride`, `GetResourceClassOverride()`, `:146,253`).
- Occupied state: `bool mIsOccupied`
  (`FGResourceNodeBase.h:266-267`, `UPROPERTY(ReplicatedUsing = OnRep_IsOccupied, BlueprintReadOnly, Category = "Resources")`),
  read via `IsOccupied()` (`:140`), set via `SetIsOccupied()` (`:138`),
  gated by `CanBecomeOccupied()` (`:142`), with a replication callback
  `OnRep_IsOccupied()` and a `OnIsOccupiedChanged` delegate (`:186-192`).
  This is a **plain bool** — it does not itself reference the occupying
  extractor (see §5).

## 2. Purity enum

Real name is **`EResourcePurity`**, not `EResourceNodePurity` (a plausible
but wrong guess) — declared `Source/FactoryGame/Public/Resources/FGResourceNode.h:26-32`:

```cpp
enum EResourcePurity
{
    RP_Inpure  UMETA( DisplayName = "Impure" ),
    RP_Normal  UMETA( DisplayName = "Normal" ),
    RP_Pure    UMETA( DisplayName = "Pure" ),
};
```

(spot-checked directly, confirmed at lines 26-30). It's a plain `UENUM`,
not `enum class`, stored as `TEnumAsByte<EResourcePurity> mPurity`
(`FGResourceNode.h:165`) with an override channel `mPurityOverride`
(`:169`). Accessor: `EResourcePurity GetResourcePurity() const` (`:113`).

There's a separate, easily-confused concept: **`EResourceAmount`**
(`FGResourceNode.h:15-22`: `RA_Poor`, `RA_Normal`, `RA_Rich`, `RA_Infinite`)
for richness/quantity — not the same axis as purity.

## 3. Enumeration / registry

- **`AFGResourceNodeManager`** (`Source/FactoryGame/Public/Resources/FGResourceNodeManager.h:94-148`),
  base `AFGSubsystem`, exposes `static AFGResourceNodeManager* Get(UWorld* world)`
  (`:99`) and holds `TArray<AFGResourceNode*> mResourceNodes` / `mGeysers`
  (`:137-138`) plus fracking maps — but these arrays are **private with no
  public getter**. Its declared purpose (comment at `:91`) is "Random Nodes
  Game Mode" support, not general-purpose enumeration. Since its `.cpp` is
  stubbed (`Get()` literally `return nullptr;` — confirmed above), whether
  it's even populated/usable at runtime is unverified and must be checked
  in-game, not assumed.
- `AFGResourceNodeUtilities` has a public
  `TArray<AFGResourceNodeBase*> mAllResourceNodesInWorld`, but it's an
  editor/`CallInEditor` utility actor for mesh assignment, not a runtime
  subsystem — unsuitable as a mod-time API.
- **SML has no existing resource-node code at all** — a recursive search of
  `Mods/SML/Source/SML` for "ResourceNode" returned zero matches. No
  manager, helper, or registry to build on there.

**Conclusion:** no confirmed, publicly-accessible enumeration API exists in
the headers available here. The evidenced approach for Phase 4's first
implementation is a plain world scan — `TActorIterator<AFGResourceNode>` or
`UGameplayStatics::GetAllActorsOfClass` — which CLAUDE.md explicitly
tolerates for "initial debug scans" while steering production code toward
subsystems/event-driven updates later. If `AFGResourceNodeManager::Get()`
turns out to return a real, populated manager at runtime (contradicting its
stubbed source), that would be a good discovery to log and document before
switching to it — but it should not be assumed from this repo's source
alone.

## 4. Stable identifiers

**None found.** `IFGSaveInterface` (`Source/FactoryGame/Public/FGSaveInterface.h:55-119`)
declares only lifecycle callbacks (`PreSaveGame`, `PostSaveGame`,
`GatherDependencies`, `ShouldSave`, `NeedTransform`) — no GUID or ID
accessor. No `FGuid`, "NetworkID", "StableId", or "PersistentId" symbol
appears anywhere under `Source/FactoryGame/Public/Resources/`.
`AFGStaticReplicatedActor` adds nothing beyond a default constructor.
Unreal's save system implicitly keys actors by level path
(`GetFName()`/`GetPathName()`), but this is not exposed as a documented,
project-sanctioned "stable ID" — using the raw actor name/path directly
would be an unverified inference, not a cited API, and CLAUDE.md's Stable
Identifiers section explicitly forbids exposing raw pointers/actor
references through the protocol regardless.

This confirms PLAN.md Phase 7's own expectation: a project-specific
identifier scheme will likely be needed. Not designing it yet, per PLAN.md
Phase 7 sequencing — flagging it here since Phase 4/5's telemetry structs
will need to carry *something* as an `id` field even before Phase 7's full
design lands (candidate stopgap: derive a session-local ID from
`GetPathName()` hashed/wrapped in a normalized struct field, clearly
documented as not save-stable, until Phase 7 replaces it — a decision to
make when Phase 5's telemetry struct is actually written, not now).

## 5. Extractor/miner association

**No back-reference from node to extractor exists.** The relationship is
one-directional (extractor → node) only:

- `AFGBuildableResourceExtractorBase::GetExtractableResource()`
  (`Source/FactoryGame/Public/Buildables/FGBuildableResourceExtractorBase.h:103`)
  returns `TScriptInterface<IFGExtractableResourceInterface> mExtractableResource`
  (`:177`).
- A deprecated legacy path, `GetResourceNode()` / `mExtractResourceNode`
  (`:99,174`), is explicitly commented "DEPRECATED - Only used for old save
  support" — do not use it for new code.
- The node side (`IFGExtractableResourceInterface`,
  `Source/FactoryGame/Public/Resources/FGExtractableResourceInterface.h:18-69`)
  only exposes the `IsOccupied()`/`SetIsOccupied()` boolean (§1) — no
  pointer back to the occupier.

To determine which extractor occupies a given node, the only evidenced
approach is enumerating `AFGBuildableResourceExtractorBase` actors and
matching each one's `GetExtractableResourceActor()` (`:129`) against the
node in question — an O(nodes × extractors) join, not a direct lookup.
Acceptable for the small numbers involved in a Satisfactory save, but worth
noting as a real cost if it needs to run frequently.

## 6. World position

No dedicated "node position" property exists on `AFGResourceNodeBase` /
`AFGResourceNode` (checked both headers for `FVector`/`Location`/`Position`
members — none found besides unrelated function parameters like
`hitLocation`). Since the class chain ultimately derives from `AActor`, the
only evidenced way to get world position is the standard
`AActor::GetActorLocation()`.

## Summary for Phase 4 implementation

| Need | API | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Enumerate nodes | `TActorIterator<AFGResourceNode>` (world scan; no working manager API found) | §3 |
| Resource type | `GetResourceClass()` | `FGResourceNodeBase.h:144` |
| Purity | `GetResourcePurity()` → `EResourcePurity` (`RP_Inpure`/`RP_Normal`/`RP_Pure`) | `FGResourceNode.h:113,26-30` |
| Occupied | `IsOccupied()` | `FGResourceNodeBase.h:140` |
| Position | `GetActorLocation()` (inherited from `AActor`) | n/a (standard Unreal API) |
| Stable ID | **Not available** — deferred to Phase 7, stopgap noted above | §4 |
| Occupying extractor | **Not directly available** — requires reverse lookup via `AFGBuildableResourceExtractorBase::GetExtractableResourceActor()` | §5 |

Everything in this table needs runtime confirmation once Phase 4's
enumeration code actually runs in-game — the header shapes are trustworthy,
the stubbed `.cpp` bodies are not.
